title: Dress-code enforcement practice - historical 2011-2016
summary: Repeated restricted counseling memoranda show how RTEC historically enforced dress/personal-appearance rules. Several core expectations are independently preserved in the current 2025 handbook, while some older restrictions are not explicitly carried forward and remain historical-only.

claims.claim: Across repeated 2011-2016 counseling memoranda, RTEC historically enforced clothing-length/coverage standards, challenged gym/sweat wear, frayed jeans, see-through or low-cut/too-short clothing, and sometimes challenged non-RTEC graphic/advertising shirts.

evidence.note: Employee identities and case specifics excluded.

claims.claim: Historical driver counseling explicitly required an RTEC name tag so clients could identify the driver and treated sweatpants/gym wear as outside the dress code; employees were sometimes given a copy of the dress policy during counseling.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2013 driver dress-code counseling record - generalized rule only
evidence.note: Current 2025 handbook independently requires drivers to wear a nametag and RTEC apparel.

claims.claim: A historical counseling memo explicitly emphasized consistent enforcement of the dress-code policy when addressing a graphic/advertising shirt.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2011 dress-code counseling record - generalized process statement

claims.claim: Historical records show repeated dress concerns could lead to stronger consequences such as being sent home/unpaid or being addressed later in performance appraisal; these are historical practice examples rather than proof of the current corrective-action sequence.

evidence.note: Current handbook independently authorizes send-home/unpaid missed time and progressive discipline.

claims.claim: The current December 15, 2025 handbook independently requires office/driver clothing to meet coverage/professional standards, prohibits ripped clothing, requires RTEC driver apparel and a driver nametag, calls for routine/consistent supervisor enforcement, and permits send-home corrective action/progressive discipline.

A 2012 historical counseling record treated bright pink hair as outside the then dress-code policy. The current 2025 handbook does not explicitly state a hair-color prohibition, so this restriction is historical-only unless another current source establishes it.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2012 dress counseling record - generalized restriction only

claims.claim: Historical counseling sometimes treated non-RTEC graphics/advertising on shirts as prohibited. The current 2025 office-attire language allows some small university/fashion-brand logos while driver attire is limited to RTEC shirts/jackets/caps, so the old logo rule must be interpreted by role and era rather than globally.

evidence.note: Historical general restriction differs from current role-specific language.
Office and driver logo rules differ.

trigger: Supervisor identifies attire/personal-appearance that may not meet the applicable dress standard.
prerequisites: Determine employee role and current dress-code section.
Consider medical/religious/ethnic or other exception request under current policy.
systems: Personnel file where counseling is documented
steps: Compare attire to role-specific current standards.
Discuss the concern and applicable rule with the employee.
decisions: Whether attire violates the current role-specific standard.
Whether repeated conduct warrants formal corrective action.
exceptions: Current handbook directs employees with medical, religious, ethnic or other unique circumstances to consult the supervisor.
controls: Use the current role-specific handbook language; do not revive historical-only appearance restrictions by analogy.
Apply standards consistently and document the actual rule relied upon.
unresolved_questions: Is there a standalone current uniform/name-tag issuance/return procedure beyond the handbook?
Are current performance appraisals ever used to document dress-code issues, or was that an older local practice?
automation_candidates: Role-specific dress-code quick reference for supervisors.
Corrective-action template that cites the exact current dress-code clause and records any exception review.

provenance.notes: Employee identities and case-level facts excluded.
